content.intro: In this lesson, you will learn **Nullable and Non-Nullable Types** as part of **Null Safety and Type Handling**. Kotlin distinguishes nullable types such as `String?` from non-null types such as `String`; callers must handle the nullable case explicitly. Use the subtopics—Declaring Nullable Types, The Role of null, Nullable Type Restrictions—as a checklist: predict what the example will do, then verify it in a project configured for the target platform.
content.why_it_matters: Functions, null safety, strings, and collections are the building blocks of most practical Kotlin code. Choosing the right operation reduces avoidable errors and makes behavior easier to test.

items.title: Declaring Nullable Types
items.text: Declaring Nullable Types is about representing or handling the possibility that a value is absent. Keep nullability visible in the type and choose an explicit fallback, branch, or result model rather than assuming the value exists.
